title: memory-fragmentation-oom-root-cause-notes-v4
content:
Summary:

Quick notes from debugging increased OOM & memory fragmentation observed in production serving builds (A/B traffic spike on 2026-03-02). Symptoms: intermittent cudaMalloc failures at peak load despite aggregate free GPU memory reported > 6GB. Errors show up as allocation failure for ~200MB blocks. Affected workloads: long-context chat models (seq_len 8k+), multi-request batching patterns, and prewarming code paths that repeatedly allocate/free per-request workspaces.

Key observations / facts:
- OOM triggered during periods of high concurrency when many short-lived allocations occur in parallel (many small allocations + occasional mid-size allocations ~100-300MB).
- nvidia-smi reports free memory but CUDA API cudaMalloc returns out-of-memory (same pattern as previous v2/v3 notes).
- Host-side allocator metrics (our rwd-alloc) show many small bins full and a small number of large uncoalesced allocations.
- Profiling (cudaMemReport + custom heap-logger) revealed lots of freed blocks that are not coalesced causing fragmentation; there are multiple pinned allocations for KV cache and workspace buffers that vary in size by model and batch.
- Stack traces for failed cudaMalloc point to fallback paths where we attempt to allocate ephemeral temporary workspaces in forward pass (linear attention precompute, fused kernels) after caching allocator returns no block.
- Enabling CUDA memory pool (cudaMemPool) and using cudaMallocAsync in an experiment reduced OOM frequency but did not eliminate fragmentation — indicates allocator behavior matters but workspace sizing & allocation pattern still cause peaks.

Root causes (hypothesis, evidence):
1) Allocation churn + mixed-size lifetime patterns -> fragmentation
   - Evidence: histograms show high rate of small alloc/free operations interleaved with medium-sized allocations that fail.
   - Repro: synthetic harness that repeatedly allocs/frees varying sizes reproduces fragmentation quickly.

2) Per-request ephemeral allocations not reused across requests (workspace per layer)
   - Evidence: code paths show workspace created/destroyed inside forward for several fused ops; arena reuse disabled in some paths for correctness reasons.

3) Backend allocator design limits coalescing of freed blocks (large-block placement is unlucky)
   - Evidence: free list snapshots show many small free segments between used large blocks. Our allocator currently bins by size and does not always merge adjacent free regions across different arenas.

4) cudaFree/cudaMalloc interactions and device synchronization points increase fragmentation risk
   - Evidence: Failing allocs usually follow stream synchronizations and cudaFree calls from other threads. CUDA driver can exhibit behavior where freed segments become non-contiguous from GPU standpoint.

5) Model workspace size variability across model versions and quantization variants
   - Evidence: A/B models with different layer fusion/conv implementation require different cudnn workspace sizes; we sometimes pick max workspace per-request leading to temporary large allocations.

Short-term mitigations tried and status:
- Pre-allocate a large contiguous pool at startup and hand out slices (slab/arena): reduced OOM events for batch-serving test by ~70% in lab. (TODO: measure tail latency impact)
- Enable cudaMallocAsync + cudaMemPool: improved allocation latency and reduced some fragmentation; needs CUDA 11.8+ and code-path gating. Works well when we can funnel all allocations through async pool.
- Limit maximum per-request workspace by capping cudnn/workspace size (set heuristics per-model): eliminated some mid-size spikes but caused occasional fallback to slower kernels.
- Reduce concurrency (throttle incoming requests) as emergency mitigation in production during incidents.

Longer-term fixes / recommendations:
1) Move to single global device memory pool (cudaMemPool) + cudaMallocAsync for all ephemeral allocations from runtime.
   - Action: prototype full-runtime mallocAsync integration, ensure streams/ownership handled correctly. Track driver version compatibility.

2) Introduce deterministic workspace sizing policy per-model/version.
   - Maintain a per-model "workspace profile" table produced by offline profiling (95th percentile required workspace for different batch sizes and seq lengths). Use profile to pre-reserve workspace slices from the pool.

3) Improve allocator to support coalescing across arenas and better placement heuristics for medium/large blocks.
   - Consider slab allocator for small bins + buddy/segregated free list for large blocks. Avoid fragmentation-prone placements for blocks > X MB.

4) Consolidate and reuse long-lived buffers (KV cache, attention caches) rather than allocating per-request.
   - Ensure KV caches are placed in separate reserved partition so they do not contribute to fragmented free space used by ephemeral allocations.

5) Stress-test harness and observability improvements (required before rollout):
- Add alloc/free traces with stack sampling to capture allocation sites and lifetimes (sampled allocation profiler).
- Heap snapshots on OOM with free-list dump and allocation histogram.
- Regression test: synthetic churn test that mimics production request interleaving. Run nightly and on PRs for runtime changes.

Practical implementation plan (phased):
Phase 0 (now):
- Keep throttle and emergency config. Add a runtime flag to force use of preallocated pool for affected hosts.
- Deploy limited experiment with cudaMallocAsync enabled on non-prod serving fleet (canary 5 hosts).

Phase 1 (2-4 weeks):
- Implement per-model workspace profile generation tool (offline profiler) and a runtime config to reserve workspace slices.
- Add sampled allocation tracing & nightly churn test.

Phase 2 (4-8 weeks):
- Integrate cudaMallocAsync + unified memory pool for ephemeral allocations. Ensure backward compatibility with hosts without driver support.
- Implement enhanced allocator improvements (coalescing and large-block placement). Add unit tests.

Phase 3 (8+ weeks):
- Fully roll out pooled allocator + workspace reservation. Monitor production OOMs and tail latency. Tune pool sizing and eviction heuristics.

Immediate next steps for owners (Ava / Jordan / Diego):
- Jordan: finish prototype using cudaMallocAsync on canary nodes and report latency/OOM metrics by EOD +3 days. (JIRA SRV-7890)
- Diego: build offline workspace profiler that runs probes across representative input shapes and emits 50/95/99 workspace size percentiles per model by EOD +1 week.
- Priya: add heap snapshot & free-list dump on OOMs to current error reporting pipeline (add artifact to linked_artifacts).

Notes / open questions:
- We need to decide pool sizing strategy: fixed reservation vs. dynamic auto-grow with eviction. Auto-grow complicates fragmentation but reduces hard OOMs.
- Verify compatibility of async allocator with current third-party libs (cuDNN/cuBLAS) and with our fused kernel launches. Some libraries use legacy cudaMallocBehavior assumptions.
- Consider running defragmentation/compaction after quiet windows (not trivial on GPU).

References & related artifacts:
- confluence:SR-3456-memory-frag (profiling dumps + previous triage)
- jira:SRV-7890 (canary experiment task)
- github:inference/runtime#456 (initial cudaMallocAsync prototype)

Rough checklist before closing this item:
- [ ] Canary config validated (no regressions in latency)
- [ ] Offline workspace profiles generated for top 20 models
- [ ] Allocator integration tests for coalescing passed
- [ ] Nightly churn test added and green for 72 hours

Notes to self (informal):
- Avoid making allocator changes in the same release as major kernel fusion changes — hard to attribute regressions.
- When profiling, use both host-side histogram and cudaMemReport; the latter often misses sub-allocator behavior.
- Remember to capture stream ids and thread ids in stack traces; cross-thread frees are common cause of weird fragmentation patterns.

End of notes.
